p:cNvPr.descr: Diagram of Receptor tyrosine kinases. Growth factor receptors that initiate signals through Tyr kinase activity include those for insulin (INSR), vascular epidermal growth factor (VEGFR), platelet-derived growth factor (PDGFR), epidermal growth factor (EGFR), high-affinity nerve growth factor (TrkA), and fibroblast growth factor (FGFR). The five receptors are shown across the outside (top) and inside (bottom) of the cell, and cross the cytoplasm and plasma membrane. Each of the structures comprise of a combination of the following: a light blue rod, which represented tyrosine kinase domain; a yellowish rod, which represents Cys-rich domain, a pinkish rod, which represents Leu-rich domain, a purple short rod, which represents Ig-like domain, and a small green circle, which represents Asp/Glu-rich region. The first receptor is INSR, which is two Leu-rich domains connected to two yellow Cys-rich domains, forming a V-shape and labeled alpha. The V-shape is connected to 4 Leu-rich domains below, which is labeled beta. The first and fourth Leu-rich domains are each connected to a Tyrosine kinase domain. The second receptor is VEGFR, made up of 7 Ig-like domains connected vertically to 2 Tyrosine kinase domains. The third receptor is PDGFR, comprised of 5 Ig-like domains vertically connected to 2 Tyrosine kinase domains. The fourth receptor is EGFR, which is represented as 2 Leu-rich domains and 2 Cys-rich domains, alternating back and forth vertically; connected on the bottom is a Tyrosine kinase domain. The fifth receptor is TrkA, which is represented by a chain of Leu-rich domain, connected to 2 Ig-like domains, connected to a blue Tyrosine kinase domain. Finally, the FGFR is represented by a chain of 1 Ig-like domain connected to 1 Asp/Glu-rich region, connected to 2 Ig-like domains, connected to 2 Tyrosine kinase domains.
